newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says China to take part in ASEAN summit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says China to take part in ASEAN summit.

text.p: Beijing will take part in the second informal summit of the Association of the Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), to be held in Malaysia in December, Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said on Monday.

Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, as chairman of ASEAN this year, will be inviting the heads of government of Japan and South Korea as well as China, Abdullah said in a statement issued by the foreign ministry.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Laos, Cambodia and Burma hope to join the grouping soon.
Dubbed the "Commemorative Summit" to celebrate the 30th anniversary of ASEAN, the meeting will bring together the heads of states of all present and prospective members, as well as invited guests.
"I very much welcome that the government of China is actively preparing for the summit," Abdullah said.
The foreign minister said he believed the summit would be able to provide further impetus to peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific region and bring regional cooperation to greater heights.
